newsitem.title: ITALY: Duce's granddaughter may join neo-fascists--paper.
newsitem.headline: Duce's granddaughter may join neo-fascists--paper.

text.p: The granddaughter of Italy's Fascist dictator Benito Mussolini is thinking of joining a neo-fascist party formed by some of the Duce's World War Two followers, La Stampa newspaper said on Sunday.
Alessandra Mussolini, who already sits in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), quit the hard right National Alliance movement last week over policy differences.

The fiery, blonde politician, 33, told La Stampa that she was giving serious thought to an offer from the neo-fascist Social Movement (MS-Fiamma) to join its ranks and hold a high office in the party.
"I shall think about it," said Mussolini, who is also a niece of screen star Sophia Loren. "I want to wake up the right."
Mussolini, who ran unsuccessfully three years ago for mayor of Naples, addressed MS-Fiamma's conference in central Italy on Saturday.
"I feel a bit like the prodigal son returning home," she told delegates. "Sorry I'm late." She said later that she had not formally joined the movement.

MS-Fiamma won around two percent of votes in Italy's general election last April. It is led by veteran Pino Rauti, who fought as a young man for Mussolini's rump fascist republic of Salo in the final months of World War Two.

Rauti formed the party after the creation in 1995 of the National Alliance. He broke ranks with National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini when Fini disbanded the neo-fascist MSI party both had belonged to in a bid for respectability and appeal.
Fini's party is part of the centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc in parliament led by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi.
